Assume full AC and its inherited countable-choice consequences. For the weighted RT functor of [[thm-weighted-rt-tqft-and-factorization]] and any complex modular ribbon fusion category, simple labels $i_1,\ldots,i_n$ and genus $g\ge0$,

$$\dim V(\Sigma_g;i_1,\ldots,i_n)=\sum_{x\in I}S_{0x}^{\,2-2g-n}\prod_{r=1}^nS_{i_rx}.$$

No complex conjugation is part of this general formula. The unmarked torus has dimension $|I|$ and basis $b_i:\mathbf1\to i\otimes i^*\subset H$. Orient its meridian/longitude basis $(m,l)$ by $\omega(m,l)=1$ and choose reference and object Lagrangian $\alpha=\lambda=\mathbb Rm$. The weight-zero positive Hopf mapping cylinder and positive core-twist cylinder have respectively the geometric classes

$$s_+=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad t=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$$

(columns are the images of $m,l$), and their operators are

$$S_{ji}=s_{ji}/D,\qquad T_{ji}=\delta_{ji}\theta_i.$$

For this positive Hopf/core-twist pair the exact relations are

$$S^2=C,\qquad(ST)^3=\kappa I,\qquad C_{ji}=\delta_{j,i^*}.$$

The inverse Hopf class is $s_-=s_+^{-1}=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ and its weight-zero operator is $S^{-1}$. That alternative pair satisfies $(S^{-1}T)^3=\kappa C$. These conventions retain the actual positive Hopf and core-twist matrices; replacing a generator by its inverse changes its geometric class. In a nonselfdual category $C$ need not be $I$.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], the mathematical scalar shell conventions of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and the second-variable-linear Hilbert pairing of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. In the fixed inertial coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] on the affine Minkowski model [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$; these coordinates have length units under [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. The parameter $\mu\ge0$ and momentum coordinate $\mathbf k$ have inverse-length units, and $\omega(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ has the same units. The parameter is not identified here with a physical rest mass. Matrix $h_D$ has inverse-length units; the dimensionless spin matrices have no physical unit assignment in this mathematical item.

Use the Pauli matrices $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. On $\mathbb C^4=\mathbb C^2\oplus\mathbb C^2$, define
$$\beta=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&0\\0&-I_2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \alpha_j=\begin{pmatrix}0&\sigma_j\\\sigma_j&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \gamma^0=\beta,\qquad \gamma^j=\beta\alpha_j.$$
For a spinor column $z\in\mathbb C^4$, its Dirac adjoint is $\bar z=z^\dagger\beta$. The Clifford contraction is $\Gamma(p):=\gamma^0p^0-\sum_{j=1}^3\gamma^jp_j$; this contraction uses the effective matrix $-\eta$ in the relation $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$.

Let $\mathcal H_D$ be the space of measurable functions $u:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb C^4$, modulo equality almost everywhere, with
$$\|u\|^2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}u(\mathbf k)^\dagger u(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}<\infty,$$
and pairing $\langle u,v\rangle=\int u(\mathbf k)^\dagger v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k/(2\pi)^3$. Define the measurable matrix $h_D(\mathbf k)=\sum_j\alpha_j k_j+\beta\mu$ and its maximal multiplication operator with domain $D(h_D)=\{u\in\mathcal H_D:h_Du\in\mathcal H_D\}$. For $\omega(\mathbf k)>0$, define the matrix fields
$$P_\pm(\mathbf k)=\frac12\left(I_4\pm\frac{h_D(\mathbf k)}{\omega(\mathbf k)}\right).$$
When $\mu=0$ at $\mathbf k=0$, set $P_+(0)=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,0)$ and $P_-(0)=\operatorname{diag}(0,I_2)$. These are complementary rank-two orthogonal projections; the value at this Lebesgue-null point does not change their multiplication operators. Write $M_{P_\pm}$ for their maximal multiplication operators and $\mathcal H_\pm=\operatorname{ran}M_{P_\pm}$. The companion matrix lemma on this page proves these are bounded orthogonal projections with closed ranges. The conjugate Hilbert space $\overline{\mathcal H_-}$ has vectors $\bar u$, scalar multiplication $z\bar u=\overline{\bar z u}$, and pairing $\langle\bar u,\bar v\rangle=\langle v,u\rangle$.

Use the sine and cosine definitions of [[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]]. For a length-coordinate increment $t\in\mathbb R$ and $\omega(\mathbf k)>0$, define the matrix multiplier
$$W_D(t,\mathbf k)=\cos(\omega t)I_4+i\frac{\sin(\omega t)}{\omega}h_D(\mathbf k).$$
At the massless apex set $W_D(t,0)=I_4$. Its unitarity, group law and generator identity are proved by the companion matrix lemma on this page.

The symbols $P_+$ and $P_-$ designate the positive- and negative-energy matrix formulas for this fixed free Dirac operator. This is purely mathematical data; no physical spin-statistics postulate or empirical assertion is included.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \langle u,v\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,$$
with the second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]; the real momentum dot product and norm are those of
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Explicitly extend the real dot product
complex-bilinearly to $a\cdot b=\sum_{j=1}^3a_jb_j$ for $a,b\in\mathbb C^3$.
Each complex fiber instead has the positive Hermitian pairing
$\langle a,b\rangle_2=\overline a\cdot b=\sum_j\overline a_jb_j$ and
norm $\|a\|^2=\sum_j|a_j|^2$; the displayed integral uses this pairing.
Hilbert completeness follows from [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For $\mathbf k\ne0$, write $n(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-n(\mathbf k)n(\mathbf k)^T.$$
Assign any value at $\mathbf k=0$, which is a Lebesgue-null set. Let $M_{P_T}$ be multiplication by this measurable matrix field and define the positive transverse photon space
$$\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T} =\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}.$$
The inner product on $\mathcal H_T$ is the restriction of that on $\mathcal H$. Each nonzero momentum fiber is the two-complex-dimensional plane $\{a\in\mathbb C^3:\mathbf k\cdot a=0\}$ perpendicular to the real vector $\mathbf k$ in that Hermitian pairing; no global continuous polarization frame is part of the definition.

Use the fixed Minkowski coordinates $x=(x^0,\mathbf x)=(ct,x^1,x^2,x^3)$, with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, on an open coordinate domain $U\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ with its standard topology. Each $x^a$ has unit metre. For a smooth scalar component $u:U\to\mathbb R$ or $u:U\to\mathbb C$, define $\partial_a u:=\partial u/\partial x^a$; thus $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$ at fixed $\mathbf x$, $\partial_j=\partial/\partial x^j$ for $j=1,2,3$, and each $\partial_a$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Raise derivative indices with $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$. The fields in this definition are smooth maps
$$\phi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R),\qquad \mathbf A\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R^3),\qquad \psi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb C^4),\qquad \chi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R).$$
Define the lower-potential component maps $A_a:U\to\mathbb R$ by $A_0=-\phi/c$ and $A_j=\mathbf A_j$; collectively $(A_a)$ is the real covector potential in this chart. Then $F_{ab}:=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a$ has smooth real component maps $F_{ab}:U\to\mathbb R$. The spinor is an ordinary commuting $\mathbb C^4$-valued map, not a tuple of Grassmann generators. Its Dirac adjoint is the smooth row-valued map $\bar\psi:=\psi^\dagger\beta:U\to(\mathbb C^4)^*$, using the fixed matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], so $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$. In fixed SI units, $\phi$ is in volts, each $A_a$ is in $\mathrm{T\,m}$, $\psi$ is assigned field dimension $\mathrm m^{-3/2}$, and $\chi$ is in webers; these unit labels accompany the maps and do not identify $q$ with a measured charge. For periodic spatial domains, the same component and unit conventions apply to smooth periodic coordinate lifts, with the quotient domain specified by the item using them.

For the SI-normalization bookkeeping, let $c>0$ (m s$^{-1}$), $\hbar>0$ (J s), $\mu_0>0$ (N A$^{-2}$), a real charge parameter $q$ (C), and a mass parameter $m>0$ (kg) be symbolic inputs; put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. In the current SI, $c$ and $h$ are defining constants while $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined; the formula below keeps $\mu_0$ symbolic and assigns it no numerical value. Use the lower-potential convention
$$A_a=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A),$$
where $A_a$ has units T m, $\phi$ is in volts, and $\mathbf A$ is in T m. Define
$$S_0=\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c},\qquad a_a=A_a/S_0,\qquad f_{ab}=\partial_aa_b-\partial_ba_a,$$
$$\mu=mc/\hbar,\qquad g=q\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}=q/\sqrt{\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a.$$
Here $D_a$ acts on $\psi\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb C^4)$ by $(D_a\psi)(x)=\partial_a\psi(x)-ig a_a(x)\psi(x)$, again a smooth map $U\to\mathbb C^4$. Thus $a_a$ and $\mu$ have units m$^{-1}$, $f_{ab}$ has units m$^{-2}$, and $g$ is dimensionless. For $\psi$ with units m$^{-3/2}$, both $-\tfrac14 f_{ab}f^{ab}$ and $\bar\psi(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi$ have units m$^{-4}$; their integral over $d^4x$ is dimensionless and represents the action divided by $\hbar$ in this normalization.

For the real smooth gauge-parameter map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R$ in webers, put $\alpha:=\chi/S_0\in C^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ (dimensionless) and use
$$A'_a=A_a+\partial_a\chi,\qquad a'_a=a_a+\partial_a\alpha,\qquad \psi'=e^{ig\alpha}\psi.$$
The induced covariant derivative is $D'_a=\partial_a-ig a'_a$. These are formal mathematical conventions for the later conditional deductions. They do not adopt a measured value of $\mu_0$, identify $q$ with an electron charge, impose charge quantization, or assert that interacting continuum fields exist.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ carry a normalized finite bounded Kraus instrument datum as defined in [[def-qft-finite-bounded-kraus-instrument]], and let $\rho$ be a density operator on $H$: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]], [[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). For each outcome $a$, put $p_a:=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal J_a(\rho))$. Then each $E_a$ is an effect ($E_a\ge0$ and $I_H-E_a\ge0$), each $\mathcal J_a(\rho)$ is positive trace class, and

$$p_a=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal J_a(\rho))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_a)\in[0,1],\qquad \sum_{a=1}^{m}p_a=1.$$

The nonselective output $\sum_a\mathcal J_a(\rho)$ is a density operator. If $p_a>0$, the normalized conditional state $\rho_a:=\mathcal J_a(\rho)/p_a$ is a density operator; when $p_a=0$, this normalized update is undefined. For a unit vector $\psi\in H$, the rank-one density operator $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ has outcome probability $p_a=\sum_{r=1}^{q_a}\|M_{a,r}\psi\|^2$. These are conditional mathematical identities; they do not assert that an apparatus realizes the instrument or supply a physical measurement postulate.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]] and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space with the second-variable-linear convention of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ define the bosonic
creation and annihilation maps $a^\dagger(h)$ and $a(h)$ and the fermionic maps
$c^\dagger(h)$ and $c(h)$ as in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. Write $a_n(h)$ and $a_n^\dagger(h)$ for
their restrictions to the $n$th bosonic sector. For bosons set

$$D(a(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge1}\|a_n(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\},\qquad D(a^\dagger(h))=\{\Psi\in\mathcal F_s(H):\sum_{n\ge0}\|a_n^\dagger(h)\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\}.$$

Then $\mathcal F_s(H)$ and $\mathcal F_a(H)$ are Hilbert spaces,
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is dense, and it is a graph core for both maximal
bosonic sector maps. The bosonic operators on their displayed domains are
closed and mutually adjoint, and on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ satisfy

$$[a(h),a^\dagger(k)]=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad [a(h),a(k)]=[a^\dagger(h),a^\dagger(k)]=0.$$

The fermionic $c(h)$ and $c^\dagger(h)$ extend to bounded operators on the
whole Fock space, with norms $\|h\|$, and satisfy on the whole space

$$\{c(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=\langle h,k\rangle_2I,\qquad \{c(h),c(k)\}=\{c^\dagger(h),c^\dagger(k)\}=0.$$

This is a mathematical construction of the two Fock representations; it does
not assign particle statistics to a physical species.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $N\ge1$, $a_1,\ldots,a_N>0$ and $c>0$. Let
$Q_{\mathrm{osc}}$ be the completion of $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^N;\mathbb C)$
for the form inner product
$$a_{\mathrm{osc}}(u,v):=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\int (\partial_j u)\overline{\partial_jv} +\int (c|q|^2+2)u\overline v.$$
This is the space $Q$ of
[[lem-qft-coercive-polynomial-form-domain]] for $V(q)=c|q|^2$ and $C_0=0$.
For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_N)\in\mathbb N_0^N$, there is a smooth product
Hermite function $\psi_{\mathbf n}$ such that
$$\langle\psi_{\mathbf n},\psi_{\mathbf m}\rangle_{L^2}=\delta_{\mathbf n\mathbf m},\qquad \overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\psi_{\mathbf n}\}=L^2(\mathbb R^N),$$
and
$$\left(-\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\partial_j^2+c|q|^2\right)\psi_{\mathbf n} =\epsilon_{\mathbf n}\psi_{\mathbf n},\qquad \epsilon_{\mathbf n}:=\sum_{j=1}^N(2n_j+1)\sqrt{a_jc}.$$
For the ground multi-index $\mathbf0$, the smooth representative is
$$\psi_{\mathbf0}(q)=\prod_{j=1}^N(b_j/\pi)^{1/4}e^{-b_jq_j^2/2}, \qquad b_j:=\sqrt{c/a_j}.$$
Each $\psi_{\mathbf n}$ belongs to $Q_{\mathrm{osc}}$, and every $u\in
Q_{\mathrm{osc}}$ satisfies the exact form expansion
$$\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\|\partial_j u\|_2^2+ c\||q|u\|_2^2 =\sum_{\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^N}\epsilon_{\mathbf n} |\langle u,\psi_{\mathbf n}\rangle|^2.$$
All parameters are positive real mathematical parameters; this lemma makes no
physical identification.

Use the transverse one-particle space $\mathcal H_T$ and multiplier $\omega(\mathbf k)$ of [[def-qft-qed-photon-energy-multiplier]], and form its symmetric Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$. Let $H_{\rm ph}:=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(\omega)$, with $\hbar,c>0$ and $d\Gamma(\omega)$ acting on the $n$-particle sector as multiplication by $\sum_{j=1}^n|\mathbf k_j|$, as in [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]]. For a coherent vector use
$$ \epsilon(f):=\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{\otimes n}}{\sqrt{n!}},\qquad C(f):=e^{-\|f\|^2/2}\epsilon(f), $$
using the tensor and direct-sum conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]].

Let $\kappa>0$. Let $b:S^2\to\mathbb C^3$ be measurable with $b\in L^2(S^2,d\Omega;\mathbb C^3)$, $\mathbf n\cdot b(\mathbf n)=0$ for a.e. $\mathbf n$, and
$$ C_b:=\int_{S^2}|b(\mathbf n)|^2\,d\Omega>0. $$
Take $\mathbf k,\kappa,\epsilon$ in inverse metres and $b$ dimensionless; then $f_\epsilon$ has momentum-wavefunction units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$, $C_b$ is dimensionless, and $\hbar c(\kappa-\epsilon)$ has energy units.
For $0<\epsilon<\kappa$, define $f_\epsilon(0)=0$ and
$$ f_\epsilon(\mathbf k):=\mathbf1_{\{\epsilon<|\mathbf k|<\kappa\}}|\mathbf k|^{-3/2}b\!\left(\frac{\mathbf k}{|\mathbf k|}\right). $$
Then
$$ \|f_\epsilon\|^2=C_b\log\frac{\kappa}{\epsilon},\qquad \langle C(f_\epsilon),H_{\rm ph}C(f_\epsilon)\rangle =\hbar c\,C_b(\kappa-\epsilon). $$
Each $C(f_\epsilon)$ is a unit vector in $D(H_{\rm ph})$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $C(f_\epsilon)\rightharpoonup0$ weakly, but the family has no strong Fock-space limit. The statement is an exact free transverse-mode construction; it asserts no interacting charged sector, continuum QED limit, or empirical observation.

Use the $(-+++)$ coordinate convention, $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$, and the Clifford matrices of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]]; the shell parameter $\mu>0$ has inverse-length units as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. For $p=(p^0,\mathbf p)\in\mathbb R^4$, write
$$ \Gamma(p):=\gamma^0p^0-\sum_{j=1}^3\gamma^jp_j,\qquad K(p):=\Gamma(p)-\mu I_4. $$
When $h(p,p)\ne\mu^2$, define the finite rational inverse
$$ S_0(p):=\frac{\Gamma(p)+\mu I_4}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}. $$
For $p,p+k$ with both denominators nonzero,
$$ S_0(p+k)\Gamma(k)S_0(p)=S_0(p)-S_0(p+k). $$
For any finite chain of off-shell momenta, the corresponding insertion differences telescope with both endpoint terms retained. If $u(p),u(p')$ satisfy $(\Gamma(p)-\mu)u(p)=0$, $(\Gamma(p')-\mu)u(p')=0$ and $p,p'$ lie on the future shell, then $\bar u(p')\Gamma(p-p')u(p)=0$, where $\bar u=u^\dagger\beta$. If $v(q)$ satisfies $(\Gamma(q)+\mu)v(q)=0$ on the future shell, then $\bar v(q)\Gamma(p+q)u(p)=0$. These are finite rational/tree identities; no Feynman boundary value, singular distribution product, loop theorem, or all-diagram gauge-independence claim is included.

Let $W\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and let
$K\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ be symmetric under interchange of its
variables. Define
$$ \Gamma_KF(\phi)=\langle K,F^{(2)}(\phi)\rangle,\qquad \alpha_K=\exp\!\left(\frac{\eta}{2}\Gamma_K\right) =\sum_{j\ge0}\frac{(\eta/2)^j}{j!}\Gamma_K^j $$
on $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)[\eta]$. Each sum is finite on each
polynomial because $\Gamma_K$ lowers degree by two. Then $\alpha_K$ is
invertible with inverse $\alpha_{-K}$, and
$$ \alpha_K(F\star_W G)=\alpha_K(F)\star_{W+K}\alpha_K(G) $$
for all regular polynomial functionals $F,G$. Thus the change from $W$
to $W+K$ is an exact algebra isomorphism on this regular class.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]].
Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open. For real
$f\in C_c^\infty(O)$ define
$$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2K_\mu f),$$
where the Segal normalization is exactly
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2$ on the finite-particle
domain, as in [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. This scale makes the self-adjoint generator
of $t\mapsto W_\mu(tf)$ equal to the closure $\overline{\Phi_\mu(f)}$,
whose restriction to $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is the real scalar field
$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the unital norm-closed operator
algebra
$$\mathfrak A_\mu(O)= \overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|} \{I,W_\mu(f),W_\mu(f)^*:f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)\}.$$
Then $O_1\subseteq O_2$ implies
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)\subseteq\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. If every difference
$x-y$, with $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$, is spacelike, then every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)$ commutes with every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. These are algebraic properties of the constructed
representation; they are not empirical signaling or measurement claims.

external_items.interface:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite measure space and let
$\boldsymbol\omega=(\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_d):X\to\mathbb R^d$ be a
finite-valued measurable map, where $d\ge1$. Put
$H=L^2(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ with the second-variable-linear pairing of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]], and form the bosonic Fock space
$\mathcal F_s(H)$. For $n\ge1$, identify $H_s^{(n)}$ with the symmetric
subspace of $L^2(X^n,\overline{\mu^{\times n}};\mathbb C)$ by iterating
[[lem-qft-l2-product-tensor-identification]]. Set $X^0=\{\star\}$,
$s_0(\star)=0$, and for $n\ge1$ set
$$s_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{r=1}^n\boldsymbol\omega(x_r)\in\mathbb R^d.$$
For $1\le j\le d$, define $H_j$ by multiplication by the $j$th coordinate
$s_{n,j}$ on sector $n$, with exact domain
$$D(H_j)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n): \sum_{n\ge1}\int_{X^n}|s_{n,j}|^2|\Psi_n|^2\,d\overline{\mu^{\times n}}<\infty\right\}.$$
Each $H_j$ is self-adjoint, and $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\cap D(H_j)$ is a
graph core. The joint projection-valued measure
[[def-projection-valued-measure]] on $\mathbb R^d$ is
$$(E(B)\Psi)_n=\mathbf1_{s_n^{-1}(B)}\Psi_n\quad(n\ge1),\qquad (E(B)\Psi)_0=\mathbf1_B(0)\Psi_0.$$
For $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, let $H_\theta$ be multiplication on sector $n$
by $\theta\cdot s_n$, with its maximal square-integrability domain. Then
$$U_\theta(t)\Psi:=\bigl(e^{it\theta\cdot s_n}\Psi_n\bigr)_{n\ge0}$$
is a strongly continuous unitary group on all of Fock space, and its norm
derivative at zero exists exactly for $\Psi\in D(H_\theta)$, where it is
$iH_\theta\Psi$. The zero-particle sector is the vacuum eigenvector at joint
value $0$.

Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Killing form $B$.
For any pair of $B$-dual bases $(x_i),(x^i)$, the tensor
$\sum_i x_i\otimes x^i\in\mathfrak g\otimes\mathfrak g$, and hence its
image $\sum_i x_ix^i\in U(\mathfrak g)$ under multiplication, is independent
of the chosen pair.

Let $H(n)$ be the Hecke tower over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ of
[[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]]. Then: (1) the elements
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ are units of $H(n)$ with
$T_i^{-1}=v^{-1}T_i+(v^{-1}-1)$; (2) the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto T_i$
descends to a group homomorphism
$$\pi_n:B_n\longrightarrow H(n)^{\times},\qquad \pi_n(\sigma_i)=T_i,$$
where $H(n)^{\times}$ is the group of units of $H(n)$; (3) for every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$\pi_n(\beta)=T_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots T_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$, and
$\pi_{n+1}(\iota_n^{\mathrm{Br}}(\beta))=\iota_n(\pi_n(\beta))$ for all
$\beta\in B_n$ under the standard inclusion of braid groups $B_n\to B_{n+1}$.

## Postulate

Adopt the following specified free-photon model in the oriented,
time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and length coordinates of
[[def-qft-framework-units]], with metric $(-,+,+,+)$ and $x^0=ct$. The
classical electromagnetic input is the smooth source-free branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the electromagnetic two-form and its potential
components are those of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and a supplied
potential is subject to [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. These EM suppliers
are physical input and conventions: they do not by themselves construct a
quantum representation.

For almost every $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, set
$\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T}$. The mathematical

Let $\Phi\colon K_0^{\mathrm{split}}(\mathrm{SBim}_n)\to H_{S_n}$ be the unique
algebra isomorphism of
[[thm-split-grothendieck-group-of-the-soergel-category-is-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]
with $\Phi([B_i])=H_i=v(T_i+1)$ and $\Phi(vX)=v\,\Phi(X)$, where $H_{S_n}$ is
the Hecke algebra over $A=\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]$ with $q=v^{-2}$ and standard
generators $T_i$, and let $\chi$ be the alternating class of
[[lem-euler-class-of-a-rouquier-complex-is-homotopy-invariant-and-multiplicative]].

(a) $\Phi(\chi(F_i))=H_i-v=v\,T_i$ and
$\Phi(\chi(F_i^{-1}))=H_i-v^{-1}=v^{-1}T_i^{-1}$; equivalently
$\chi(F_i(-1))$ maps to $T_i$ and $\chi(F_i^{-1}(1))$ maps to $T_i^{-1}$. In
particular $\chi(F_i)\chi(F_i^{-1})=1$, and the powers of $v$ are the exact
normalization of the library's shift convention, not an ambiguity.

(b) For every braid $\beta\in B_n$ and every signed word $\sigma$ for $\beta$,
$\Phi(\chi(F(\sigma)))=v^{e(\sigma)}T_\beta$, where
$T_\beta:=T_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots T_{i_r}^{\epsilon_r}$ is the image of
$\beta$ under the standard group homomorphism $B_n\to H_{S_n}^{\times}$,
$\sigma_i\mapsto T_i$, and
$e(\sigma)=\#\{\epsilon_k=1\}-\#\{\epsilon_k=-1\}$ depends only on $\beta$.
Hence $\beta\mapsto v^{-e(\beta)}\chi(F(\beta))$, composed with $\Phi$, is that
standard homomorphism: up to the grading normalization, the Rouquier complex of
a braid decategorifies to the image of the braid in the Hecke algebra.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. On $\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}$ let $u(x)=1/(16\pi^4|x|^4)$, equivalently the square of the displayed Euclidean kernel $C_0(x)=1/(4\pi^2|x|^2)$; interpret $u$ as its regular distribution there. Choose $\chi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$ equal to one near $0$. For $\mu>0$ define

$$T_\mu(\varphi):=\int_{\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}}\frac{\varphi(x)-\chi(\mu x)\varphi(0)}{16\pi^4|x|^4}\,d^4x.$$

Then $T_\mu$ is a distribution extending $u$, has scaling degree $4$, and for every $\mu,\nu>0$,

$$T_\mu-T_\nu=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\log(\mu/\nu)\,\delta_0.$$

In particular, no extension of $u$ with scaling degree $4$ is exactly homogeneous, where exact homogeneity means $\rho^4T_\rho=T$ for every $\rho>0$. Coordinates use one fixed Euclidean unit; if units are assigned, $\mu$ and $\nu$ have reciprocal coordinate units, so the logarithm's ratio is dimensionless. This is a Euclidean distribution identity and does not identify a measured coupling or physical beta function.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge1$, let $t\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\})$ have finite real scaling degree $\delta$, and let $\mathcal E_\delta(t)$ be the set of its extensions in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$ having scaling degree exactly $\delta$. This set is nonempty by [[thm-qft-finite-scaling-degree-extension]]. If $\delta<n$, then $\mathcal E_\delta(t)$ has exactly one member. If $\delta\ge n$, let $k$ be the unique nonnegative integer with $k\le\delta-n<k+1$ (the floor of $\delta-n$). Then, for any $T_0\in\mathcal E_\delta(t)$,

$$\mathcal E_\delta(t)=T_0+\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{\partial^\alpha\delta_0:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$

Here a **point-local counterterm** means a distribution whose support, as defined in [[def-support-of-a-distribution]], is contained in $\{0\}$. Thus the same-degree freedom is finite dimensional, with precisely the displayed delta derivatives as its basis; at the threshold $\delta=n$, only a multiple of $\delta_0$ is allowed.

Hall algebra,
$$A_{\mathrm{all}}=\prod_{\phi\in\Phi_Z\ \mathrm{decreasing}}S_Z(\phi),\qquad \Phi_Z=\{\phi_Z(\mathbf e):0\ne\mathbf e\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}\}.$$

$$R=\sum_i(f_i\otimes1_H)\otimes(\varepsilon_H\otimes h_i)$$

is basis-independent and invertible, with

$$R^{-1}=\sum_i(f_i\otimes1_H)\otimes(\varepsilon_H\otimes S^{-1}(h_i)).$$

It is quasitriangular in the convention

$$R\Delta_D(d)=\Delta_D^{\mathrm{op}}(d)R,\qquad(\Delta_D\otimes\operatorname{id})R=R_{13}R_{23},\qquad\alpha^{-1}_{D,D,D}(\operatorname{id}\otimes\Delta_D)R=R_{13}R_{12}.$$

On every pair of left $D(H)$-modules, $\tau\circ R$ is the Yetter–Drinfeld braiding of [[thm-hh-double-modules-and-yetter-drinfeld-modules]].

This is a conditional mathematical theorem about the prescribed current and
free coherent-state construction defined below, under the exact supplier
interfaces [F2] and [L1]. Here “soft current” is only a name for the displayed
rational function: no scattering-amplitude factorization or approximation
claim is made. The weak-zero and no-strong-limit conclusions are conditional
on [L1]; the projective-ray conclusion is proved separately in step 7.1.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the constants and conventions of
[[def-qft-example-data]], and that the two supplier interfaces [F2]
and [L1] hold exactly as stated below. Let $I$ be a finite, possibly empty,
set of leg labels. A leg $i\in I$ carries an energy $E_i>0$ in joules,
a dimensionless velocity $v_i=\mathbf v_{i,\rm phys}/c\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$\mathbf v_{i,\rm phys}$ in m s$^{-1}$ and
$|v_i|<1$, a dimensionless charge number $Q_i\in\mathbb R$ (physical charge
$eQ_i$ coulombs), and an orientation sign $\eta_i\in\{-1,1\}$, with
$\eta_i=-1$ for an incoming leg and $+1$ for an outgoing leg. Require charge
balance $\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i=0$. Use
$h=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ and
$h(a,b)=a^0b^0-\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b$ for algebraic four-vector
contractions. For $n\in S^2:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ and energy
$\omega>0$ in joules, put
$$ p_i=E_i(1,v_i),\qquad q=\omega(1,n),\qquad K:S^2\to\mathbb R^4,\quad K(n)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\frac{(1,v_i)}{1-v_i\cdot n}. $$
Each $p_i$ has positive energy and
$h(p_i,p_i)=E_i^2(1-|v_i|^2)>0$; this timelike condition is the precise
meaning of “massive” here, with rest mass
$m_i=E_i\sqrt{1-|v_i|^2}/c^2>0$. The prescribed current is the function
$J(q)=\sum_{i\in I}\eta_iQ_i\,p_i/h(p_i,q)$ on
$\{\omega(1,n):\omega>0,\ n\in S^2\}$. Since
$h(p_i,q)=E_i\omega(1-v_i\cdot n)>0$, this equals $K(n)/\omega$.
Thus $K$ is dimensionless and $J(q)$ has units $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
Write $K(n)=(K^0(n),\mathbf K(n))$, let $P_T(n)=I-n\otimes n$, and
$K_\perp(n)=P_T(n)\mathbf K(n)$. Define $d\Omega$ as Euclidean chart
surface measure on $S^2$ and
$$ C=\frac{g^2}{2(2\pi)^3}\int_{S^2}|K_\perp(n)|^2\,d\Omega(n)\ge0. $$
Here $g>0$ is the dimensionless coupling of [[def-qft-example-data]] and
$\lambda,\Lambda$ are energy cutoffs in joules. Write $\mathbf q=\omega n$
for the spatial energy coordinate, distinct from the four-vector
$q=(\omega,\mathbf q)$ above. For $\mathbf q\ne0$, put $\omega=|\mathbf q|$
and $n=\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|$ and define
$$ h_\lambda(\mathbf q)=g\frac{K_\perp(n)}{\omega}\mathbf1_{\{\lambda<\omega<\Lambda\}},\qquad 0<\lambda<\Lambda; $$
Set $h_\lambda(0)=0$ and regard $h_\lambda$ as a function of $\mathbf q$.
Define
$\mathcal H_{E,T}:=\{h\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf q|];\mathbb C^3):\mathbf q\cdot h(\mathbf q)=0\ {\rm a.e.}\}$,
with the componentwise Hermitian integral pairing linear in its second
variable. On this energy-coordinate transverse Hilbert space the exact norm is
$$ N_\lambda=\|h_\lambda\|^2=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda). $$
The energy-coordinate wavefunction has units $\mathrm J^{-1}$ and its
one-particle measure has units $\mathrm J^2$, so $N_\lambda$ and $C$ are
dimensionless; its value at $q=0$ is immaterial to this $L^2$ vector.
Under the canonical unitary $U:\mathcal H_{E,T}\to\mathcal H_T$ specified and proved in step 3.1,
the same vector is represented by the length-coordinate vector $f_\lambda$
defined as follows. Set $f_\lambda(0)=0$ and, for $k\ne0$, define
$$ f_\lambda(k)=\mathbf1_{\{\lambda/(\hbar c)<|k|<\Lambda/(\hbar c)\}} |k|^{-3/2}b(k/|k|),\qquad b(n)=\frac{gK_\perp(n)}{\sqrt{2(2\pi)^3}},\qquad \int_{S^2}|b|^2\,d\Omega=C. $$
Here $b$ is dimensionless and the $L^2(d^3k)$ wavefunction $f_\lambda$ has
units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$.
The normalized coherent vector
$\Psi_\lambda=W(-i\sqrt2 f_\lambda)\Omega
=\exp(-N_\lambda/2)\epsilon(f_\lambda)$ has squared norm in sector $m$
$$ s_m=\exp(-N_\lambda)\frac{N_\lambda^m}{m!},\qquad \sum_{m\ge0}s_m=1,\qquad \sum_{m\ge0}m s_m=N_\lambda, $$
with $N_\lambda^0=1$ also when $N_\lambda=0$.
These are Hilbert-space sector norms and their index sum; no measured
probability is asserted. For the free photon energy operator
$H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|k|)$, $\Psi_\lambda$ is in its operator domain
and its quadratic expectation is $C(\Lambda-\lambda)$ joules.

If $C=0$, $f_\lambda=0$ almost everywhere and $\Psi_\lambda=\Omega$ for each
cutoff. If $C>0$, the exact hypotheses of the current [L1] hold with
$\epsilon=\lambda/(\hbar c)$, $\kappa=\Lambda/(\hbar c)$ and the displayed
nonzero transverse angular function $b$. Conditional on [L1], the family has
no strong Fock-vector limit and converges weakly to zero, while its free
energy expectation stays bounded. For a unit Fock vector $u$, define its
projective ray $[u]:=\{zu:z\in\mathbb C,\ |z|=1\}$. For unit vectors $u,v$
define their projective-ray distance by
$d([u],[v]):=\inf_{|z|=1}\|u-zv\|$. This is a metric on phase classes: symmetry follows by replacing $z$ with
$\overline z$, the triangle inequality follows from the norm triangle
inequality and phase invariance, and compactness of the unit circle makes zero
distance equivalent to equality of the classes. Projective convergence means convergence in this
distance, equivalently norm convergence to a fixed unit vector after allowing
a unit-modulus phase at each cutoff. Step 7.1 proves separately that
these rays have no projective limit, including after arbitrary phase choices. This is
not a result about full interacting QED, universal charged sectors,
detector-inclusive observables, or measured photon statistics.

Let $X=\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $W\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ be
any continuous complex bidistribution. For a real formal parameter $\eta$
and $F,G\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)$, define
$$ F\star_W G=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{\eta^k}{k!}\left\langle W^{\otimes k},F^{(k)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(k)}(\phi)\right\rangle . $$
The pairing is over $k$ independent pairs of variables; $W^{\otimes k}$
is formed by iterated distributional tensor products, not by multiplying
distributions at coincident points. The sum is finite because the inputs are
polynomial. It defines an element of
$\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)[\eta]$, and $\star_W$ is associative.
Here complex conjugation is $\overline{a+ib}=a-ib$ for $a,b\in\mathbb R$.
If $W$ is Hermitian in the sense
$\overline{\langle W,\overline g\otimes\overline f\rangle}
=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle$, then
$(F\star_W G)^*=G^*\star_W F^*$, where $F^*(\phi)=\overline{F(\phi)}$.
For $\ell_f(\phi)=\int_X f(x)\phi(x)\,dx$,
$$ [\ell_f,\ell_g]_{\star_W}=\eta\bigl(W(f,g)-W(g,f)\bigr), \qquad W(f,g):=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle . $$

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let
$(W_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a positive tempered moment family on $T(S)$ as in
[[def-qft-positive-tempered-moments]]. Write $\omega$ for its linear extension,
and let $P^\uparrow_+$, $T_g$, and $\alpha_g$ be the group and pullbacks of
[[def-qft-poincare-test-action]] and
[[lem-qft-poincare-pullback-continuity-on-schwartz]]. Let
$(H_\omega,D_\omega,\pi_\omega,\Omega_\omega)$ be the GNS construction of
[[thm-qft-algebraic-gns-domain]] for this functional, with the first-variable-
linear Hilbert pairing.

For $f\in S$, put $X(f):=f$ in degree one and
$\Phi(f):=\pi_\omega(X(f))|_{D_\omega}$. Then $D_\omega$ is a common invariant
dense domain, every $\Phi(f)$ is closable with
$\Phi(\overline f)=\Phi(f)^*|_{D_\omega}$, and $\Phi$ is a weak
operator-valued tempered distribution in the exact sense of
[[def-qft-weak-operator-valued-tempered-distribution]]. Its vacuum moments are
exactly the input:
$$\bigl(\Phi(f_1)\cdots\Phi(f_n)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega\bigr)=\langle W_n,J_n(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n)\rangle.$$

The following additional conclusions are conditional on additional moment
identities.

1. If $\omega\circ\alpha_g=\omega$ for every $g\in P^\uparrow_+$, then there
is a strongly continuous unitary representation $g\mapsto U_g$ on
$H_\omega$ fixing $\Omega_\omega$ and satisfying
$$U_g\Phi(f)U_g^{-1}|_{D_\omega}=\Phi(T_gf)\qquad(g\in P^\uparrow_+,\ f\in S).$$

2. Let $f,h\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C)$ be
the complex test functions of [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]],
viewed as elements of $S$ under the canonical inclusion of
[[lem-test-function-inclusion-in-schwartz-space-is-continuous]]. In this
definition, $\operatorname{supp}f$ and $\operatorname{supp}h$ are the closures
in $\mathbb R^4$ of their nonzero sets and hence compact. If these supports
are spacelike separated, meaning $(x^0-y^0)^2-|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2<0$ for every
$x\in\operatorname{supp}f$, $y\in\operatorname{supp}h$, and
$$\omega\bigl(b^*[X(f),X(h)]a\bigr)=0\qquad(a,b\in T(S)),$$
then $[\Phi(f),\Phi(h)]=0$ on $D_\omega$. More generally, any polynomial
relation $r\in T(S)$ satisfying $\omega(b^*ra)=0$ for all $a,b\in T(S)$ is
represented by $\pi_\omega(r)=0$ on $D_\omega$; tested field equations are
instances of this statement when their required identities are assumed.

3. For translations $\tau_z=(I,z)$ define
$$D_{b,a}(z):=\omega\bigl(b^*\alpha_{\tau_z}(a)\bigr)\qquad(a,b\in T(S)).$$
If $\omega$ is translation-invariant, each $D_{b,a}$ is a bounded continuous
function and hence a regular tempered distribution; applying the
symmetry-implementation lemma to the translation subgroup gives strongly
continuous unitaries $U_{\tau_z}$. If, in addition,
$\operatorname{supp}\widehat{D}_{b,a,M}\subseteq\overline V_+$ for every $a,b$,
with the Fourier convention of
[[def-qft-minkowski-fourier-transform]], then the reconstructed translation
matrix coefficients
$$z\longmapsto\bigl(U_{\tau_z}\pi_\omega(a)\Omega_\omega,\pi_\omega(b)\Omega_\omega\bigr)$$
have precisely the same Fourier support. This is a matrix-coefficient
spectrum condition; it does not assert joint self-adjoint energy-momentum
generators or their joint spectral measure.

This theorem reconstructs a weak field only from supplied, actually positive
continuous moments. It does not construct an unspecified positive functional,
complete a formal perturbation series, or establish the full Wightman
reconstruction theorem with assumptions not listed here.

Assume AC. Let $T$ be a bounded normal operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert
space $H$, with operator spectrum $\sigma(T)$
([[def-spectrum-and-resolvent-of-a-bounded-operator]]). Then:

1. there is a unique regular projection valued measure $E$ on the Borel
   $\sigma$-algebra of the nonempty compact set $\sigma(T)\subseteq\mathbb C$
   such that $\int z\,dE(z)=T$ and, equivalently,
   $$\Phi_E(f)=f(T)\qquad\text{for every continuous }f:\sigma(T)\to\mathbb C,$$
   where $f(T)$ is the continuous functional calculus of
   [[thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-normal-operators]] and
   $\Phi_E$ is the bounded Borel integral of the projection valued measure $E$;
   this $E$ is the **spectral projection valued measure** of $T$;
2. conversely, if $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb C$ is nonempty and compact and $E$ is
   a regular projection valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of
   $\Lambda$, then $T_E:=\int z\,dE(z)=\Phi_E(z)$ is a bounded normal operator
   with $\sigma(T_E)\subseteq\Lambda$ and $\|T_E\|\le\max_{z\in\Lambda}|z|$.

$$Z(M,n;\lambda)^j_i=\kappa^{n+a(R_M;\lambda,\alpha)-\sigma(B)}D^{-m-1+\chi(\Sigma_{\rm out})/2}d(j)F_0(\Omega;i,j).$$

Here $F_0$ is the finite colored graph operator with the disconnected-boundary unit-channel projections of [[lem-rt-capped-operator-normalization-and-composition]], and $d(j)$ is the product of outgoing handle-color dimensions. For every compatible circle cut there is a natural factorization isomorphism

$$V(\Sigma_{\rm glued};\vec W)\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I}V(\Sigma_{\rm cut};\vec W,i,i^*).$$

The sewing map from right to left is the actual normalized tube map; its inverse is the complete composition-dual cutting resolution. Both separating and nonseparating cuts, all multiplicities, commuting disjoint cuts and iterated gluing are included. Markings, tensor order and the Lagrangian identifications of the cut are retained; a change of parametrization is represented by its weighted mapping cylinder.

planned_interfaces.proof_route: First show the difference is symmetric; symmetry reverses the future relation into the past relation, whose intersection is empty, so its wavefront is empty. For each finite polynomial degree expand contractions and verify the intertwiner by the binomial identity. Specify microcausal derivative wavefront exclusions and compact support; no product on the diagonal is inferred without the wavefront check.

planned_interfaces.interface: The diagonal product δ_0² is not furnished by the wavefront product theorem: WF(δ_0) contains opposite nonzero covectors. A mollifier square has mass proportional to ε^{-n}, and no distribution limit exists without subtraction.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Compute ∫ε^{-2n}ρ(x/ε)²f(x)dx=ε^{-n}∫ρ(y)²f(εy)dy for nonnegative ρ and f=1 near zero.

planned_interfaces.interface: On flat four-dimensional Minkowski space take compactly supported local polynomial scalar functionals, formal parameters g and ℏ, and the off-shell free field algebra. A renormalization prescription is a family T_n, T_0=1,T_1 fixed, satisfying symmetry, causal factorization, translation covariance, field independence, the stated scaling bound, and formal unitarity. Gauge identities are additional conditions.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Specify variational derivative wavefronts, relative coordinates at each total diagonal, anti-time-ordering and involution. No positivity of formal coefficients is assumed.

planned_interfaces.interface: For the stated free scalar polynomial algebra, time-ordered products satisfying the scalar contract can be constructed at every finite order; at each graph order the extension ambiguity is a finite linear combination of derivatives of delta distributions on relevant diagonals, bounded by the specified scaling degree. This yields a formal series, with no convergence or adiabatic limit assertion.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Induct in n: causal-order open sets cover the complement of the total diagonal; lower-order factorizations agree on overlaps by associativity/locality. Glue using a locally finite partition of unity, reduce to relative coordinates, extend each numerical distribution by the scaling-degree theorem, symmetrize and impose scalar normalization conditions. Prove the needed finite graph scaling bounds using derivative kernel estimates. Partial diagonals are already resolved by the induction, not independently multiplied. Lorentz covariance needs the finite-dimensional cocycle correction proved locally; include it as part of this theorem proof rather than assume it.

planned_interfaces.interface: Given two admissible scalar time-ordered systems S and S′ with the same first-order normalization, there is a unique local formal map Z(V)=V+O(V²), Z(0)=0, Z′(0)=id, such that S′=S∘Z. Composition and recursively defined formal inverse preserve the local support and normalization conditions.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: At homogeneous order n subtract all known lower partitions; the difference is supported on the total diagonal. Define Z_n to be that local difference with exact factorial conventions. Composition uses finite partitions of n, hence is coefficientwise finite. Invert recursively, showing the leading unknown occurs linearly.

planned_interfaces.interface: In four dimensions the two-vertex four-point scalar graph has scaling degree four in its relative variable; its renormalized extension may differ by cδ. The scale difference is local, not a numerical scattering probability.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Use the old exact Euclidean log residue as a worked normalization example; keep the Euclidean kernel distinct from its Lorentzian boundary-value counterpart.

planned_interfaces.interface: H is the polynomial algebra over Q on finite nonempty rooted trees, graded by vertices. Δ(t)=t⊗1+1⊗t+Σ_c P_c(t)⊗R_c(t), summing cuts with at most one cut edge on each root-to-leaf path; extend Δ multiplicatively. ε kills positive degree. This is a rooted-tree subtraction model, not an automatic Hopf algebra of every gauge graph.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Define the empty forest unit, trunk and pruned forest, and distinguish full cut from empty cut to avoid double counting.

planned_interfaces.interface: The rooted-forest coproduct is coassociative and H is a connected graded bialgebra. Its antipode is S(t)=−t−Σ_c S(P_c(t))R_c(t), extended by the convolution inverse, and this recursion terminates in every fixed degree.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Identify iterated coproduct terms with two-level nested prunings of a tree; both orders encode the same three layers. All proper factors have fewer vertices, so degree induction yields both convolution inverse identities. Prove multiplicativity of the antipode in the commutative case.

planned_interfaces.interface: Let A=A_-⊕A_+ be a commutative Laurent-series algebra split into negative powers and nonnegative powers, with projection R onto A_-. For a character φ:H→A, set φ_-(t)=−R[φ(t)+Σ_c φ_-(P_c(t))φ(R_c(t))] and φ_+=φ_-*φ. Then φ_- and φ_+ are characters, φ_+ takes positive-degree values in A_+, and the recursion is degreewise finite.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Verify R(a)R(b)=R(R(a)b+aR(b)−ab) directly by the Laurent splitting. Use this identity and the multiplicative coproduct to prove by degree induction that the recursion preserves products. Expand φ_+ and cancel the negative part; this is the exact Hopf utilization in subtraction, without importing an unproved full Feynman-graph identification.

planned_interfaces.interface: For the two-vertex ladder t with one proper cut and one-vertex tree τ, φ_-(t)=−R(φ(t)+φ_-(τ)φ(τ)); subtracting only Rφ(t) generally differs.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Choose φ(τ)=a/ε+b and φ(t)=c/ε²+d/ε+e and calculate the a²/ε² and ab/ε corrections explicitly.

planned_interfaces.interface: On the graded-commutative algebra of finite jets of a U(1) connection A, odd ghost c, antighost cbar and even auxiliary B, define sA=dc, sc=0, scbar=B,sB=0, and commute s with spacetime derivatives. On a charged matter field ψ of charge q set sψ=iqcψ and use the graded Leibniz rule. Work off shell with explicit ghost numbers.

planned_interfaces.interface: The stated Abelian s squares to zero. Adjoining finitely many jet doublets su=v,sv=0 independent of the other transformations does not change polynomial BRST cohomology: every closed expression of strictly positive doublet degree is exact.

planned_interfaces.interface: If a nilpotent BRST Ward identity first fails at formal order ℏ^n by a local ghost-number-one integrated functional A, the nilpotence identity forces sA=0 modulo total derivatives. A local counterterm cancels this failure exactly when [A]=0 in H^1(s|d), with the sign fixed by the chosen Ward convention.

Conversely a cohomologically trivial representative supplies that counterterm. This proves the obstruction principle conditional on locality of the breaking; the quantum action principle is an additional theorem obligation in a gauge model, not a consequence of scalar extension.

An anomaly-cancellation statement requires a regulator/renormalization construction that identifies the local consistent anomaly with the descent class of this tensor, specifies mixed gravitational and global anomalies separately, and carries all loop hypotheses. planned_interfaces.interface: Let K be a positive self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space with spectrum in [M²,∞), M>0, and let J be a vector. In a finite regulator, integrate a real Gaussian heavy coordinate χ with quadratic action 〈χ,Kχ〉/2−〈J,χ〉. Its normalized elimination contributes −〈J,K^{-1}J〉/2 to the effective action. planned_interfaces.interface: Let K=M²+A with A≥0 self-adjoint and J in its spectral subspace 0≤A≤E². For N≥0, K^{-1}J=M^{-2}Σ_{r=0}^N(−A/M²)^rJ+R_NJ, with ||R_NJ||≤M^{-2}(E²/M²)^{N+1}||J||. Consequently the induced quadratic-action remainder is at most ||J||²( E²/M²)^{N+1}/(2M²). AC is inherited from the analytic construction suppliers.

Then exp(−(V_{C_1})_{C_2})=exp(−V_{C_1+C_2}); additive vacuum constants follow the chosen normalization. AC is inherited from the analytic construction suppliers.

planned_interfaces.interface: Let σ_ρ be the engineering-scaling automorphism of the specified formal scalar S-matrix algebra, ρ>0. Define Z_ρ by σ_ρ S σ_ρ^{-1}=S∘Z_ρ when both systems obey the causal normalization contract. Z_ρ is a formal local map, not a physical measurement of running charge.

planned_interfaces.interface: For the model beta equation dg/dt=bg², real initial g_0, its solution is g(t)=g_0/(1−bg_0t) on the maximal interval avoiding its pole. Under an invertible formal scheme change g′=g+ag²+O(g³), the leading beta coefficient b is unchanged. The pole is a property of this truncated equation, not a theorem about an ultraviolet completion.
planned_interfaces.proof_route: Differentiate the rational expression and use uniqueness by separation or a direct reciprocal calculation on intervals where g≠0; include the zero solution. Compute β′=(dg′/dg)β and re-expand in g′ through quadratic order.

The rescaling (λ,λtilde)↦(tλ,t^{-1}λtilde), t≠0, leaves momentum invariant. An outgoing helicity-h amplitude has weight t^{-2h}. Angle and square brackets use fixed alternating tensors.

planned_interfaces.interface: Let A(z) be a rational shifted tree amplitude, regular at z=0, with only simple finite factorization poles z_i and A(z)→0 as z→∞. Then A(0)=−Σ_i Res_{z=z_i} A(z)/z. A boundary term is required when decay fails.

Construct the two-line spinor shift preserving nullness and total momentum. Insert the assumed factorization residues; proving factorization and large-z behavior for a chosen Lagrangian is a separate model obligation.

planned_interfaces.interface: For a massless vector polarization defined with a reference spinor having nonzero denominator, changing the reference changes the polarization by a scalar multiple of its momentum. Therefore contraction with a conserved on-shell tree current is reference independent.

planned_interfaces.interface: For an explicitly prescribed conserved eikonal current and cutoffs 0<ε<Δ<Λ, take a free-photon coherent state whose mode intensity is dν=C dω/ω on the selected angular region, C≥0. planned_interfaces.proof_route: Differentiate or compare positive powers for two resolutions.

planned_interfaces.interface: On a smooth oriented time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian spacetime without boundary, let P be a real normally hyperbolic formally self-adjoint scalar operator. Retarded and advanced Green maps E± act on compact smooth tests, satisfy PE±=E±P=id there and have future/past causal support; E=E−−E+ fixes the symplectic sign convention.

Prove compactness by global hyperbolicity and check signs against E−−E+. Prove injectivity by extending the local Cauchy solution uniquely, rather than assume it for arbitrary noncausal embeddings.

planned_interfaces.proof_route: For a fixed finite sequence, its quadratic form has finitely many distribution pairings, each convergent, so take the limit of nonnegative real numbers. Test each covariance equality before taking the limit. No interchange of an infinite sum or large-distance limit is made.

planned_interfaces.interface: For m>0 and f compactly supported at positive Euclidean time, C=(−Δ+m²)^{-1} has reflected quadratic form ∫d^{d−1}k/(2π)^{d−1}(2ω_k)^{-1}|∫_0∞e^{−ω_kt} fhat(t,k)dt|²≥0. Its Gaussian moment hierarchy is reflection positive.

Reflection changes t−s to t+s, producing a squared Laplace transform. A north-regular helicity frame differs from e_σ by a phase removing its north-pole singularity. In that gauge a vortex coefficient e^{iℓφ} has integer ℓ; exact J_z labels include the frame contribution.
